title: PUBLIC WORKS COMMITTEE REPORT relative to identifying funding for Watershed Protection Division illegal dumping investigations and enforcement.
text:
[Council File 24-1178]
[Items for which Public Hearings Have Been Held]
PUBLIC WORKS COMMITTEE REPORT relative to identifying funding for Watershed Protection Division illegal dumping investigations and enforcement.
Recommendation(s) for Council action:
1. DIRECT the Chief Administrative Officer (CAO), in coordination with the Bureau of Sanitation (BOS) and the Chief Legislative Analyst (CLA), to identify appropriate funding sources and authorize the allocation of the necessary resources, for Illegal Dumping enforcement, depending on the level of service desired by Council. The report should also provide recommendations for establishing a tiered structure for illegal dumping fines and penalties that considers distinctions between individuals and commercial entities, businesses, or corporations.
2. REQUEST the City Attorney, in coordination with the BOS, CAO, CLA, and other relevant departments, to report in 90 days on the feasibility of amending the Los Angeles Municipal Code to increase fines and penalties for illegal dumping, ensuring they exceed the cost of collection services and implementing higher fines for repeat violations to strengthen deterrence.
3. INSTRUCT the CAO, with the assistance of the Bureau of Street Services, BOS, and City Attorney, to report on fines and penalties collected for illegal dumping, including the total revenue generated, the distribution of revenues among City funds, and any legal or regulatory requirements governing the allocation and use of these funds.
Fiscal Impact Statement:
None reported by the BOS. Neither the CAO nor the CLA has completed a financial analysis of this report.
Community Impact Statement:
Yes For: Downtown Los Angeles Neighborhood Council
summary: The Bureau of Sanitation is to report on how to fund illegal dumping investigations and enforcement by the Watershed Protection Division.
